title: Exploring the Potential of Mesenchymal Stem Cell Sheet on The Development of Hepatocellular Carcinoma In Vivo
protocol: Coat the culture dishes with undiluted fetal bovine serum (FBS) and ensure to cover all the surface of the dish.
Incubate the dishes for 24 h at 37 °C in a humidified atmosphere containing 5% CO2 and 95% air.
Remove the excess FBS from the coated dishes and allow the dishes to dry at room temperature (RT) for at least 1 h.
Prepare the three cell suspensions: 1 x 10^6 HepG2 cells, 1 x 10^6 HepG2 cells with BMMSCs, and 1 x 10^6 HepG2 cells with UCMSCs (in a ratio of 4:1 for both BMMSCs and UCMSCs).
Seed the appropriate cell suspension to each labeled dish.
Suspend all cells in DMEM culture medium supplemented with 10% FBS and 1% penicillin/streptomycin.
Incubate the cells at 37 °C in a humidified atmosphere containing 5% CO2 and 95% air.
At 100% cell confluence, take the dishes out of the 37 °C incubator.
Incubate the HepG2 cell sheet dish for 1 h at room temperature.
Incubate the HepG2/BMMSC and HepG2/UCMSC cell sheet dishes for 30 - 40 min at 20 °C in a humidified atmosphere containing 5% CO2 and 95% air.
Conduct all surgical procedures in a sterile separate area within the laboratory, such as a hood, laminar flow cabinet, or an aseptic surgery room.
Ensure that all surfaces of the surgery area are non-porous, sealed, durable, and sanitizable.
Wear proper protective gear, including scrubs, gloves, facemasks, and head and shoe covers.
Use surgical tools that are clean and sterilized via autoclaving at the beginning of the surgery.
Change gloves between rats.
Prepare injectable anesthesia for rats using ketamine-xylazine.
Mix 2 mL of ketamine with 1 mL of xylazine (at a concentration of 20 mg/mL) in a sterile 10-mL serum collection vial.
Add 1 mL of sterile physiologic saline to the mixture.
Shake well before use.
Inject 0.2 mL of ketamine-xylazine solution per 100 g of body weight intraperitoneally.
Remove visible dirt/debris from the surgical site.
Check the depth of anesthesia by testing the pedal withdrawal reflex (foot pad pinch on both hind feet).
Disinfect the surgery area with a two-stage scrub using povidone-iodine/isopropanol.
Cover the rat with a sterile drape to avoid contamination of the incision.
Inject rats subcutaneously with buprenorphine (0.01 - 0.05 mg/kg) prior to making the incision.
Make a 7- to 10-cm cut between the skins and underlying muscles using a sterile scalpel to expose the liver.
Separate the abdominal muscle from the skin with the flat back edge of the scalpel.
Carefully stab the linea alba using a scalpel and extend the cut with sharp scissors.
Collect the cell sheet from the culture dish.
Gently tap the culture dish over the bench to detach the sheet from its surface.
Separate the cell sheet from the dish's surface by scraping the edge of the sheet in a half circle using a sterile pipette tip.
Gently remove the entire medium from the culture dish.
Ensure the sheet is intact without any damage; otherwise, it cannot be used.
Soak a sterile membrane (filter paper) with normal saline.
Remove excess saline from the membrane using a sterile cotton pad.
Place the wet membrane over the cell sheet to avoid creases and air bubbles.
Add few drops of normal saline over the membrane and the cell sheet for easier collection.
Avoid breaking the cell sheet by not using cold saline.
Collect the membrane with forceps after ensuring the cell sheet is properly attached.
Make sure the liver surface is dry by gently tapping it with a sterile cotton pad.
Place the membrane with the cell sheet over a single lobe of the rat's liver using sterile forceps.
Add few drops of sterile saline and apply gentle pressure to detach the cell sheet from the membrane.
Wait for 5 min before carefully removing the membrane.
Close the underlying muscles and skin incisions with 5-0 nylon sutures.
House the rat individually immediately after surgery to avoid cannibalism or suffocation.
Monitor the rat regularly until it is conscious and fully ambulant.
Assess the rats daily for 5 - 14 days post-surgery to ensure no complications.
Check that the wound is closed and sutures are intact without being excessively tight.
Ensure there are no signs of infection at the incision site such as heat, excessive swelling, or purulent discharge.
Look for signs associated with pain such as decreased food and water consumption, weight loss, dehydration, skin tenting, or rapid and open mouth breathing.
Inject rats subcutaneously with buprenorphine (0.01 - 0.05 mg/kg) every 6 - 8 hours if moderate to severe post-surgery pain is observed.
Continue the pain control treatment for a minimum of 48 - 72 hours postoperatively.
Scarifice the rat one month after transplantation.
Collect the transplanted area for histological and immunohistochemical analysis.
